children: Fervo Energy shares were higher in premarket trading after the said it signed major deal to supply power to Alphabet's Google from a Utah project.
Shares climbed by about 13% ahead of the morning bell to $17.38 following a Wall Street Journal report confirming the contract.

Under the terms of the contract, its largest ever, the geothermal company will provide 396 megawatts of electricity to Google starting in 2028, with Google holding an option to expand the contract by an additional 600 megawatts through mid-2030.
The power will supply a planned Google data center in Utah from its Cape Station project in the state.
Google is part of a tech-sector-wide race to build out the massive infrastructure to run next-generation artificial intelligence and cloud demand.

Fervo said the purchase power agreement supports its continued build-out of its $2 billion Cape Station geothermal facility, where the first phase remains on track to begin delivering electricity to the grid later this year.
